verdict.tagline: Haunting psychological horror with a brilliant soundtrack and deep emotional pull.

you appreciate a phenomenal atmospheric soundtrack
you enjoy immersive turn based adventures

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as slow and basic.

citations.review_text: I don't get how this game has overwhelmingly positive reviews. Genuinely just a waste of money. The combat is so slow, and it's basic as well. The dialogue is also sluggish. Everything is just so slow, you get a little breath of gameplay besides the combat and then 10 seconds later it's just another cutscene. It's actually like doing a chore. If the combat were just better I'd consider this game playable but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ It's actually equivalent to cutting your balls off.

2/5
I am personally not a fan of the turn-based combat system. I heard the story picks up later in the game but it feels flat to me at the start. I respect the creators though, I can tell they put a lot of thought and effort into it, especially with the animation. If you like Deltarune you will probably like this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the soundtrack as a standout feature of the game.

citations.review_text: Got it as a birthday gift from a friend, it’s a good game, but the soundtrack is even better :)

SPOILERS!!!

I played the full game on my switch and have done both routes and this game is extremely important to me, the writing is amazing, the art style at first comes across as a cute game yet later on the psychological horror themes along with the art style mix perfectly, i have suffered with depression since i was a child and it perfectly portrays depression, never ending guilt and learning to accept and forgive yourself. I cried my eyes out at final duet, the music is beautiful and really makes you feel what the game wants you to. The character dynamics between the main group is beautiful, they're all different in their own ways yet contrast with each other beautifully, I relate to two characters in the game, being Sunny and Aubrey, My sister unfortunately took her life while i was little, i miss her everyday and wish i could see the person she had become to this day, after that day i isolated myself, my grades significantly dropped and i had started keeping to myself instead of constantly talking like i used to, i became very angry at everything, I hated everyone and everything, I was constantly yelling at people, I was severely jealous of people who still had their siblings and I hate when they fight because I would do anything for my older sister back.
I love the contrast between head space and the real world, head space its very childish with its aspects and colouring, the people around you it feels like a big day dream, The real world the colours become less saturated and it shows how everyone's grown up especially after Maris' passing.
I 100% recommend everyone plays this game at some point in their life, this game has a massive impact on my life and has a special place for it

(i ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love air conditioning......)

Enjoyed this game way more than I expected. Favorite things about the game had to be the soundtrack and story, and I'm already a fan of RPG's so I already expected the combat to be good. 9/10 Totally recommend if you're into RPG's.

[h1] Tepid and boring. Don't be fooled by the "Overwhelmingly Positive" rating. [/h1]

I really, really tried to fall in love with this. I really did. Because, from what I heard, Omori is a f*cked up game that will have you balling your eyes out at the very end. The concept alone piqued my interest.

But all it really did was leave me disappointed.

The story itself is nothing to complain about. Sure, there's a lot to be desired about it but all in all it handles itself pretty well. 

The only gripe I had with the story was the ending. It had ZERO business being that anticlimactic after all the build up that happened toward the end.

The main focus of my critique is the gameplay itself. It is so unbelievably boring and mind numbing that after I finished it I was left wondering what else I could've done during the 30 or so hours that I spent with this game.

I could've read a book, maybe did something productive with my life! But instead, I devoted my time and energy on a bunch of filler and encountering enemies that I have no intention of fighting whatsoever.

I was already bored during the first couple of hours of playing since the gameplay loop makes it feel more like a chore than something actually enjoyable. But I persisted, I stayed put. Because the reviews showed promise, and like a gambler I clung on to the chance that maybe, JUST MAYBE, I'll find something worthwhile toward the end.

And that brings us back to the story.

If you remember what I just mentioned before, I said the story was nothing to complain about.

Well, that would be the case if the gameplay wasn't so painfully lukewarm.

The times you spend between the real world and the dream world are so astronomical that when you get to the juicy, supposedly gut-wrenching parts of the story, all the anticipation you've had about it have already shriveled up since you spend most of your time killing bunnies and other goofy creatures in the dream world. 

Also, there's just TOO MUCH SH!T on this game. Lik…

omori is a game you should be playing at least twice (and personally i couldn't handle any more than that):
on your first playthrough, you should be completely unaware of the plot (in hopes that you haven't gotten any spoilers) just learning the mechanics of the game and uncovering everything alongside sunny/omori and the characters in the game themselves
and on the second run, with prior knowledge of the game you'd have the opportunity to look around and notice every single little detail actually has a meaning - EVEN the ones that might seem to little to even take into consideration and that makes the game even more beautiful and meaningful (but also 100 times more depressing than it already is) 
overall i think omori is a beautifully written game that deserves all the praise it gets and even the things you might think of as nuisances (like the repetitive combat and how debatably long it takes) EVERYTHING has a good reason for it and EVERYTHING has been thought of. therefore to appreciate the writing even further i believe it should be played at least twice :3

Let's start with the negative:
- The story made no sense. It's not bad, but illogical.
- The battles are repetative. 
- You can't walk diagonally, which doesn't seem like a big deal, but is quite annoying
- The game is stretched out with unnecessary battles a lot.
- The Ending is literally 3 hours of pure story non-stop. Sure, the story was hinted at before, but it should have been integrated into the main game more. Feels like the creators of this game got bored creating levels and just wanted to finish the game.
- Missing variety. If there are 5 doors in the scene, interacting with any of them will generate the same response. Maybe I played undertale too much, but that's kinda disappointing.

With that out of the way, here is why you won't regret buying the game:
- The artstyle is amazing
- The music is amazing
- The visual effects are amazing
- The battle-system is unique. It could be more flexible to not be repetative, but it's still pretty good.
- There are mild jumpscares, but not too many. It keeps you alert and invested.
- Even though the story is illogical, it's still relly good. It sucks you in, you want to know what happenens next.
- The game implies and hints at things, without spilling them out literally. It doesn't think you were stupid, like most modern games seem to.
- I really liked the psychological aspect of some of the scenes (don't want to spoil it for you)
- The boss-battles are balanced. You need to think/strategize in order to win.

8/10

This is one of the greatest games I've ever played. I was hesitant at first because I knew it was a slow-burner, and I knew it would take a while to pick up, but I heard too many great things about this game, and forced myself to play. I'm glad I did, because I unknowingly spent hours in the game; every new location feels completely different. The story is great, emotional, has an insane plot twist, and the gameplay is addicting. 8/10 heavily recommend

I first played this game when it came out and have since played it quite a few times. Hehe, on here and my switch. 

Visually, the game is nostalgic and lovable, the sketched out drawings holding so much heart in them, and the soundtrack bringing me to tears or having me jumping in my seat plenty of times. 

The battle system is really enjoyable especially the incorporations of "emotions" into fights, the only issue with the gameplay itself is that the game is Quite long and can have slow pacing at some points. For me, that wasn't a big issue because I just love to be in the world of OMORI! 

I somewhat used the game itself as escapism from, ironically, trauma and amnesia + related mental issues I was experiencing, but this game is genuinely what got me through it all. I have grown and changed from someone who was nearly the same as Sunny, to someone who takes risks and ventures further into reality everyday, and this game continues to inspire me and drive me forward to always face my fears and do right by the people I love. 

If you have been through similar things, sought out a dreamlike world to get away from your stress, and found that you can never run too far from what you are so afraid of... Play this game. I love every character, every dialogue, and every moment where you get closer to the horrifying truth that fuels this fantastical and quirky world. Take care of yourself, all it costs is your love!
